expectations.text: A persistent onboarding guide is written as REPO_GUIDE.md at the repo root, covering structure, auth, data storage and how to run/test.
expectations.evidence: Wrote ONBOARDING_GUIDE.md (248 lines) to outputs only; there's no REPO_GUIDE.md in the repo root. A persistent guide does exist, so this mostly tests the skill's naming and location convention.

expectations.text: The auth explanation traces the real flow with file references: the Authorization header accepts both `Token` and `Bearer` (src/app/routes/auth/auth.ts), express-jwt `auth.required`/`auth.optional` middleware populates `req.auth.user.id`, tokens are signed in token.utils.ts with a 60d expiry, and passwords are hashed/compared with bcryptjs in auth.service.ts.
expectations.evidence: Section 3: Token or Bearer accepted by getTokenFromHeaders, express-jwt sets req.auth, so handlers read req.auth?.user?.id; jwt.sign with expiresIn '60d' (token.utils.ts:3-6); bcrypt. Citations use short paths (auth.ts:16,21).

expectations.text: The output flags the hard-coded `'superSecret'` fallback for JWT_SECRET as a security risk or gotcha.
expectations.evidence: Secret handling paragraph plus Gotcha #2: JWT_SECRET falls back to 'superSecret' in three places, anyone can forge tokens.

expectations.text: The data model section correctly states Prisma with PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL and names the four models User, Article, Comment and Tag with their key relations (follows, favorites, article tags), citing src/prisma/schema.prisma.
expectations.evidence: Section 4: PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL, schema.prisma; ASCII relation diagram with User/Article/Comment/Tag, _ArticleToTag, UserFavorites, UserFollows; model table.

expectations.text: Run instructions use only commands that exist in the repo (e.g. npm install, npx prisma generate, npx prisma migrate deploy, npx nx serve api, npx prisma db seed, npx nx test) and invent no nonexistent npm scripts such as `npm run dev`.
expectations.evidence: Commands: npm ci, npx prisma generate/migrate deploy/db seed, npx nx serve api, npx nx e2e e2e, plus a docker run for a local Postgres (helper, not a claimed repo script). No invented npm scripts.

expectations.text: The output explains that unit tests in src/tests mock Prisma with jest-mock-extended (src/tests/prisma-mock.ts) so no database is needed, distinct from the e2e tests in e2e/ that need a running server.
expectations.evidence: Explains that prisma-mock.ts uses jest.mock + mockDeep, and that e2e needs a running server. It also verified by running the suite that 7 of 27 unit tests fail because of import order, which is stronger evidence than the with-skill run's unverified suspicion.

expectations.text: The deliverables cite at least 15 repo file paths, and every cited path and line number resolves (check_paths.py reports no broken references).
expectations.evidence: check_paths.py: 55 references, all resolve (many are short bare filenames like auth.ts:16 that resolve via a unique-name search); 20 file:line citations, meeting the threshold of 15.

expectations.text: The run did not install dependencies or execute repo code: there is no node_modules directory in the run's checkout.
expectations.evidence: It ran npm ci, prisma generate/migrate/seed, built and started the server, ran the unit tests and lint, and started a Postgres Docker container, all inside a scratch copy (work/verify). The checkout itself has no node_modules, so the literal sub-check passes, but the assertion's main clause (did not install or execute repo code) fails.
